title: A Butterfly the Weight of a Paper Clip Flies Nearly 3,000 Miles

scenes.text: A butterfly lighter than a paper clip flies almost three thousand miles.
Every autumn, monarchs from Canada and the northern United States head south to Mexico.
The butterflies making the trip have never been there. Their ancestors flew it the year before.
In spring, it takes four generations to fly back north.
That tiny body weighs less than a gram.
Less than a paper clip. Almost three thousand miles.

description:
A monarch butterfly weighs less than a paper clip, yet some fly almost 3,000 miles to winter in Mexico.
The ones that make the trip south have never been there. It takes four generations to come back north.
Have you ever seen a monarch?
first_comment: Bonus: no single monarch flies the whole loop. It takes four generations to come back north. Have you ever seen one in your garden?
